$comment: ★ TF-C111 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION P3): `library.pe` is now ucrtbase.dll — this file moved with the whole co-state group (malloc/stdlib/string/stdio/io/errno/direct/process/sys-stat in ONE commit), because <io.h> OWNS the CRT fd table that stdio is layered on and an fd minted by one runtime is meaningless to the other. Every symbol below is a MEASURED ucrtbase.dll export (`objdump -p C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll`) EXCEPT the FIND pair, which needed the rename below; the older dumpbin msvcrt ordinals quoted further down are retained as the c98/c106 provenance record, NOT as the current binding. ★★ THE FIND-PAIR RENAME, and the TRAP it avoids: the plain `_wfindfirst`/`_wfindnext` are msvcrt-ONLY (ucrtbase exports neither), so the flip would have broken every pe binary's LOAD at 0xC0000139 (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT). The symbols are therefore `_wfindfirst64i32`/`_wfindnext64i32`, with the legacy spellings kept alive as pe MACROS — which is not an invention but EXACTLY what MSVC's own corecrt_wio.h does (`#define _wfindfirst _wfindfirst64i32` under the default undefined `_USE_32BIT_TIME_T`). The `64i32` suffix is LOAD-BEARING and must not be 'simplified' to `_wfindfirst64`: BOTH DLLs export the plain-`64` names too, so that spelling would resolve and link cleanly — and then write a 64-bit `size` into the 32-bit `_fsize_t` field of the struct below, shifting the 520-byte `name` array and overrunning the caller's record. Silent corruption, not a link error (the same shape as the `_fstat64i32` trap that cost this project a 0xC0000409). `64i32` == TIME64 timestamps + a 32-bit size, which is EXACTLY the `_wfinddata_t` pe variant already declared here (`struct _wfinddata64i32_t`, corecrt_wio.h) — so the rename is a pure symbol-name edit with ZERO struct churn. | c106: +the FIND family (_wfindfirst/_wfindnext/_findclose + _wfinddata_t) + _pclose(FILE*) + _fileno + _A_* attribute constants (corecrt_io.h). ★ x64 ABI (c106-audit runtime-probed C:\Windows\System32\msvcrt.dll via P/Invoke, 0xCC-sentinel buffer): the PLAIN _wfindfirst/_wfindnext exports are the _wfinddata64i32_t shape — TIME64 (not time32; x64 msvcrt never had a 32-bit-time era, so the 'legacy names = time32' lore is x86-32-only) with a size32 field: {attrib u32@0, [pad4], time_create i64@8, time_access i64@16, time_write i64@24, size u32@32, name wchar[260]@36}, sizeof 560 (align 8). The natural-alignment engine derives the @4 pad + the @32 size + @36 name; a time32 (540B, name@20) descriptor read garbage names AND overran the shim's stack _wfinddata_t by 16B on names >=252 wchars. sqlite's windirent shim (shell.c:4030) reads data.name/data.attrib. |Neutral shipped <io.h> (Microsoft CRT low-level I/O) — c98 (Windows-host sub-arc, the 3-header F001A batch). shell.c includes it twice on the pe route: line ~239 (the _WIN32 CLI prologue that maps isatty->_isatty, access->_access, unlink->_unlink) and line ~383 (the sqlite3_stdio.c Windows section: _setmode on console/file streams). The ACTIVE amalgamation surface is exactly: _isatty (IsConsole/UseWtext probes), _access (the access() macro), _unlink (the unlink macro), _setmode (sqlite3_fsetmode/UTF-16 console modes), plus the wide twins shellDeleteFile uses directly (_wunlink + _waccess, shell.c ~30869) and fileio_chmod uses (_wchmod, ~9942); _chmod ships as the trivial narrow pair of _wchmod. NOT shipped (unused on the active pe route): _open/_close/_read/_write/_lseek and the _findfirst family — the _wfindfirst/_wfindnext references sit in the windirent block which is `_MSC_VER`-gated (since c105's MSVC-profile flip (_MSC_VER=1943) that block IS the intended live path -- the _wfindfirst64/_wfindnext64 question re-derives when the c106 shell.c batch probes it); no F001A-driven need, and the _O_* mode CONSTANTS (_O_TEXT/_O_BINARY/_O_U8TEXT...) belong to <fcntl.h> per the Windows SDK layout, NOT here (they are the next semantic wave, not this header's provenance). `availableObjectFormats:[pe]` — a Microsoft-CRT header fails loud on elf/macho. `library:{pe:msvcrt.dll}` — all eight are msvcrt.dll exports (verified via dumpbin /exports: _access 171, _chmod 213, _isatty 401, _setmode 726, _unlink 847, _waccess 906, _wchmod 912, _wunlink 1050), NOT kernel32. SIGNATURES (Microsoft SDK corecrt_io.h/corecrt_wio.h): int _access(const char*,int); int _chmod(const char*,int); int _unlink(const char*); int _isatty(int); int _setmode(int,int); the wide forms take const wchar_t* — Windows wchar_t is UTF-16 u16 (== windows.json's WCHAR), so they spell ptr<u16>. NOTE: stddef.json currently ships the FORMAT-NEUTRAL `wchar_t` typedef as i32 (the glibc width) with no pe variant — a pe caller declaring `wchar_t*` therefore mismatches ptr<u16> until stddef.json gains a per-format variant; these signatures stay SDK-TRUE rather than mirroring that latent width gap. | pe64 full-source testfixture (D-SQLITE-PE64-TESTFIXTURE-FRONTEND B3): the low-level POSIX-name I/O surface the sqlite test modules reach through <io.h>. (a) _open/_close/_read + the MSVC <io.h> non-stdc-name MACROS open->_open, close->_close, read->_read (the _CRT_DECLARE_NONSTDC_NAMES convention) — test_fs.c (fstree vtab) reaches <io.h> transitively via windirent.h and calls bare open((const char*)...,O_RDONLY)/close(fd)/read(fd,buf,n). Signatures per corecrt_io.h: `int _open(const char*,int,...)` (variadic mode arg), `int _close(int)`, `int _read(int,void*,unsigned int)` (msvcrt _read count is unsigned int + int return, NOT the POSIX size_t/ssize_t). (b) _commit + _chsize_s — test_quota.c (the pe quota-VFS path, includes <io.h> directly) calls `_commit(_fileno(f))` and `_chsize_s(_fileno(f),szNew)`: `int _commit(int)`, `errno_t _chsize_s(int,__int64)` -> fn(i32,i64)->i32. (c) the intptr_t typedef — MSVC <io.h> transitively provides it (corecrt.h) and fileio.c's windirent DIRENT struct declares `intptr_t d_handle` (the _findfirst handle); BYTE-IDENTICAL to stdint.json's definition (the per-dataModel `long`/`long long` identity vocabulary) so the name-first-wins dedup + D-LANG-TYPE-IDENTITY-VOCABULARY check pass when a TU pulls both <io.h> and <stdint.h>. All six symbols are dumpbin/objdump-verified real msvcrt.dll exports (_open 670, _close 218, _read 691, _commit 219, _chsize_s 214, _fileno 293). | ★★★ LANE-CFG — THE POSIX (oldnames) SPELLINGS THIS HEADER OWNS, so that `<unistd.h>` can be a real RE-EXPORT on pe instead of an assertion. ✔MEASURED, not inferred: a per-header probe against the same-platform oracle `C:/Strawberry/c/bin/x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc` (`-dumpmachine` = x86_64-w64-mingw32) — one TU each, `#include <io.h>` + `void *p = (void*)&NAME;`, rc read directly — shows mingw's <io.h> ALONE declares close read write lseek unlink rmdir access getcwd chdir isatty dup dup2. THREE were already served here as macros (open->_open, close->_close, read->_read, kept untouched); EIGHT are added: write lseek access isatty unlink rmdir chdir getcwd. ★★ THEY ARE SYMBOL ROWS WITH A FLAT `linkName`, NOT MACROS, AND THE CHOICE IS THE REFERENCE-TRUE ONE. mingw declares them as ordinary FUNCTIONS (io.h:219 unlink, :280 chdir, :281 getcwd, :284 rmdir, :327 access, :332 dup, :333 dup2, :336 isatty, :338 lseek, :346 write) and binds each to the underscored CRT export through oldnames — which is precisely what `linkName` expresses (declare the C identifier, name the export it decorates; pe64's `cSymbolDecoration.scheme` is `none`, so `_write` composes to exactly `_write`). A `#define write _write` would ALSO rewrite every struct member, field and local spelled `write` in every TU that includes this header — a hazard mingw does not have and this file should not add. ★ SIGNATURES ARE THE MSVC/mingw ONES, NOT THE POSIX ONES, because these names ARE the CRT functions: `int write(int,const void*,unsigned int)` (io.h:346 — unsigned count and int return, NOT size_t/ssize_t), `long lseek(int,long,int)` (io.h:338 — LLP64 `long` is 32-bit, so the tagged i32 "long" spelling, and a >2GB offset needs _lseeki64, deliberately not shipped without a consumer), `char *getcwd(char*,int)` (io.h:281 — int, matching direct.json's _getcwd twin), and the plain `int f(const char*)` / `int f(int)` shapes for the rest. ★ EAGER-IMPORT SAFETY ([[D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT]]) MEASURED BEFORE SHIPPING: `objdump -p C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll`, 4340 name-table entries, exact-match grep — _write _lseek _access _isatty _unlink _rmdir _chdir _getcwd are ALL PRESENT, and the un-underscored POSIX spellings (write read close lseek access isatty unlink rmdir chdir getcwd) are ALL ABSENT, which is exactly why the linkName is required rather than optional. ★ NOT SHIPPED, deliberately: dup/dup2 (mingw declares them, ucrtbase exports _dup/_dup2, no consumer — this directory ships on a consumer); and the `_write`/`_lseek` underscore twins themselves (declaring both spellings would emit TWO eager imports for ONE export, the `environ`/`__environ` lesson). ★★ FULL-FILE CENSUS AGAINST THE ORACLE (every row, every surface kind — the discipline that opening a header on a new format forces): all 26 symbols, 6 constants, 2 typedefs, 1 struct and 5 macros were probed with a `#include <io.h>` TU. CONCURRING: _access _waccess _chmod _wchmod _unlink _wunlink _isatty _setmode _wfindfirst64i32 _wfindnext64i32 _findclose _open _close _read _commit _chsize_s + the 8 new POSIX rows, the six _A_* constants, `wchar_t`, `intptr_t`, `struct _wfinddata_t`, and the `_wfindfirst`/`_wfindnext` macros. TWO DIVERGENCES, both REPORTED rather than fixed because each is a judgement call, not a mechanical gate: (a) `_fileno` and `_pclose` are NOT in mingw's <io.h> — ✔MEASURED, they are `<stdio.h>` names on mingw exactly as they are in MSVC's SDK, and a `#include <io.h>` TU taking their address FAILS while the same TU over <stdio.h> compiles. This file over-declares them; the honest fix is to MOVE both rows to stdio.json, which is a placement change on a live sqlite-pe64 path (shell.c reaches `_pclose` through this header today) and so belongs to whoever can re-gate that corpus. (b) The `open`/`close`/`read` MACROS are not macros on mingw at all — ✔MEASURED, `#ifndef open / #error` compiles clean there, because mingw declares all three as ordinary FUNCTIONS. They should become `linkName` symbol rows like their eight new siblings, which would also end this file's split personality (three names realized as text substitution, eight as declarations); deliberately not done in the same edit that introduced the eight, so a regression on the sqlite pe64 path cannot be ambiguous about which change caused it. ★★★ SECOND LANE-CFG PASS (operator: NO WORKAROUNDS). (a) `open`/`close`/`read` CONVERTED FROM MACROS TO `linkName` SYMBOL ROWS. ✔MEASURED: `#ifndef open / #error` compiles clean under the oracle, i.e. mingw declares all three as ORDINARY FUNCTIONS, not macros. The difference is observable, not stylistic — a macro changes what `#ifndef` answers, makes `&open` unspellable, and rewrites every unrelated identifier of that spelling in the TU; the corpus witness now takes `&open`/`&close`/`&read` precisely so a silent regression to macros cannot pass. (b) `dup`/`dup2` + the `_dup`/`_dup2` twins, `_umask`, `_chsize` added — all mingw <io.h> declarations, all measured ucrtbase exports. (c) F_OK/X_OK/W_OK/R_OK ADDED HERE, where mingw puts them (io.h:182-185); the references DISAGREE (MSVC's <io.h> has none of them) and the tie is broken by the identity DSS claims on this format, which is MinGW. Placing them here rather than duplicating unistd.json's rows is also what keeps ONE name out of the pe closure twice. (d) `_fileno`/`_pclose` REMOVED — ✔MEASURED they are <stdio.h> names on mingw AND in the MSVC SDK: a `#include <io.h>` TU taking their address FAILS while the same TU over <stdio.h> compiles. They now live in stdio.json, pe-gated. | ★ P56 lane sv ([[D-FFI-SHIPPED-DESCRIPTORS-DECLARE-STRUCTS-THEIR-OWN-SIGNATURES-DO-NOT-USE]]) — TWO OF THIS FILE'S FIVE `ptr<void>` SIGNATURE SLOTS WERE THE DEFECT AND THREE WERE ALWAYS CORRECT, which is the whole census in one descriptor. `_wfindfirst64i32` and `_wfindnext64i32` now take `ptr<_wfinddata_t>`, the struct this file already declared; `_read`, `read` and `write` KEEP `ptr<void>` because their buffer parameter genuinely is `void *`. ✔SETTLED BY BOTH pe REFERENCES, read rather than assumed: the Windows SDK's corecrt_wio.h declares `intptr_t _wfindfirst64i32(wchar_t const*, struct _wfinddata64i32_t*)` with `#define _wfinddata_t _wfinddata64i32_t`, and mingw-w64's io.h declares the same pair. ✔LAYOUT RE-MEASURED BY EXECUTION with mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 native: 560 B align 8 — attrib u32@0, time_create i64@8, time_access i64@16, time_write i64@24, size i32@32, name wchar_t[260]@36 (520 B) — matching the declared variant exactly. ★★ THE AGREEMENT IS NOW COMPILER-CHECKED ON EVERY pe BUILD AND NEEDED NO EDIT TO THE BODY: DSS's own shipped realization `runtime/platform/src/dirent.c` already calls `_wfindfirst64i32(pattern, &d->data)` with a `struct _wfinddata_t data;` member, so retyping the descriptor binds the ABI DSS publishes to the bytes DSS writes — mutate either and that translation unit stops compiling.
$typeAliasSpellingComment: D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-TYPE-ALIAS-SPELLING-KEYED-ON-DATA-MODEL-ALONE (P48 lane st, 2026-09-01): `intptr_t`'s variant selector was `when:{dataModel}` ALONE, on a TWO-WORLD assumption with a THIRD world under it (Darwin is LP64 yet spells `uint64_t` `unsigned long long` while keeping `intptr_t` `long`). Every such arm now names BOTH axes, `when:{dataModel,format}`; the measurement lives ONCE in `stdint.json`'s `$comment`. THIS FILE GETS ONE ARM, NOT THREE, and that is the point of the new key rather than an omission: `availableObjectFormats` is [pe], so the LP64 arm that stood here was UNREACHABLE - dead config asserting an `<io.h>` spelling for platforms that have no `<io.h>`. Under the old `dataModel`-only key that dead arm was indistinguishable from a live one. MEASURED on pe (mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 and MSVC 19.51.36252 agree): `intptr_t` is `long long`. If this header is ever un-gated to another format, 0 arms match there and the typedef fails LOUD as undefined rather than silently inheriting glibc's spelling.
